routes.name: Tourist stay, visa-exempt nationalities (Category A)
routes.summary: Category A countries (visa exempt) enter as tourists without a visa. Tourists can stay up to 90 days, extendable once, with a 180 day cap from entry. The country list is not in the regulation, so check with IGM.

other: Category A is set by visa-waiver agreements or by the national migration authority. The country list was not readable on the official pages I could open.

stay.note: One extension only, total stay cannot exceed 180 days from entry.

routes.name: Central American entry with ID or passport
routes.summary: Central Americans can enter as tourists with an original national ID or a valid passport, subject to reciprocity. Stay is up to 90 days, extendable once.

other: Subject to reciprocity.
Which countries count and how this ties to the CA-4 agreement was not confirmed on a source I could open.

routes.name: Tourist or traveler consular visa (Category B countries)
routes.summary: Citizens of Category B countries apply for a visa at a Guatemalan embassy or consulate. A single entry visa lasts 6 to 12 months and a multiple entry visa 1 to 5 years. Stay is up to 90 days, extendable once.

other: Needs the visa form, valid passport, travel itinerary, income proof or bank statements for the last 3 months (Spanish or English), and an international credit card (a debit card needs 3 months of statements).
A service request letter is needed only for paid consulting or advisory work.
Consulates may ask for an interview, in person or virtual.
Category B nationals with a valid US, Mexico, Canada or Schengen visa do not need this visa.
The Category B country list was not on the page I read.

stay.note: Extendable once, total cannot exceed 180 days from entry. Visa validity: single entry 6 to 12 months, multiple entry 1 to 5 years.

routes.name: Tourist or traveler consulted visa (Category C countries)
routes.summary: Citizens of Category C countries need a visa that IGM approves first, then issued through a Guatemalan consulate. A Guatemalan guarantor is required. IGM must decide within 30 days once the file is complete.

other: Needs the form, passport copy, police record from home country, a Guatemalan guarantor with proof of income, and hotel and tour bookings or an invitation letter.
Applications go to IGM Extranjeria in Guatemala.
The Category C country list was not on the page I read.

routes.processing: IGM resolves complete Category C applications within 30 days.

routes.name: Visa-exempt entry for Category B nationals with a US, Mexico, Canada or Schengen visa
routes.summary: Category B nationals who hold a valid visa for the United States, Mexico, Canada or a Schengen country are treated as Category A and do not need a Guatemalan visa.

other: Applies to Category B nationals. The regulation does not extend this to Category C.

stay.note: Standard tourist rule, extendable once, 180 day cap from entry.

routes.name: Paid consulting stay (up to 180 days)
routes.summary: Category C nationals hired for paid consulting or advisory work apply through IGM with a service request letter stating the pay. The Migration Code allows up to 180 days as a traveler.

other: Needs a Guatemalan guarantor, a service request letter naming the pay, company registry papers for private hirers, and tax filings.
The 180 day limit comes from the Code, which I did not re-read in this pass.

routes.name: Temporary residence, migrant worker (Guatemalan employer)
routes.summary: Temporary residence for foreigners with a job offer from a Guatemalan employer. It is granted for up to 5 years, based on the offer term. You need a Guatemalan guarantor and a work permit from the Labor Ministry within 3 months.

other: Original job offer letter with position, hours, term, pay, start date and workplace.
Guatemalan guarantor letter, not needed for state employers.
Work permit from the Ministry of Labor within 3 months of the approval, renewed yearly.
Apply 30 days before expiry to renew.

stay.note: 1 to 5 years, set by the job offer term. Over 5 years means applying for permanent residence.

routes.name: Temporary residence, investor
routes.summary: Temporary residence of 1 to 5 years for foreigners who are part of a business and/or invest US$100,000 in movable or immovable property. You file a sworn notarial statement of the planned activity.

other: Sworn notarial statement of the economic activity and expected length of stay.
Renewal needs a sworn statement that the activity continues, with proof.
Dependents follow the migrant worker rules.

investment.note: In commercial entities and/or movable or immovable property. Proof can be registry certificates, share titles, equipment invoices and source of funds.

routes.name: Temporary residence, student
routes.summary: Student residence lasts for the school cycle or university course and can be renewed for as long as studies last. Children of a resident applicant can also qualify.

other: Current enrollment, recent registration proof or acceptance letter from a recognized school or university in Guatemala.
Proof of funds, a scholarship or a financing commitment from you or a sponsor.
Renewal needs proof of studies done and that they continue.

stay.note: As long as the course lasts.

routes.name: Temporary residence, athletes, artists, researchers, religious ministers
routes.summary: Athletes and artists get residence for the length of their contract, up to 5 years. Researchers, scientists and intellectuals need a contract and guarantor. Religious ministers need a letter from a religious authority in Guatemala.

other: Athletes: titles, federation membership and club or committee approval of the contract.
Artists: job offer letter and Guatemalan guarantor.
Researchers, scientists, intellectuals: qualification proof, guarantor and a current contract.
Ministers: letter from the religious authority, plus legal status of the church unless Catholic.

routes.name: Permanent residence for rentistas and pensioners
routes.summary: Foreigners with steady lawful income from abroad can get permanent residence as a rentista or pensioner, without doing paid work in Guatemala. The minimum is US$1,250 a month, plus US$300 for each dependent.

other: Cannot do paid work in Guatemala under this status.
Every 5 years you must show the income continues.
Permanent residence is open ended.

income.note: Plus US$300 a month for each dependent (spouse, unmarried children, minors). Income must come from abroad. Rentista income: foreign bank deposits or investments, foreign business investments, real estate remittances, or certain Guatemalan bonds bought with foreign currency. Pensioner: retirement, widow, orphan, disability or social security pay.

routes.name: Permanent residence after 5 years of temporary residence
routes.summary: Temporary residents with 5 years or more of residence can apply for permanent residence. You file a sworn statement of your activity and a current guarantor letter, unless you held religious minister status.

other: 5 years or more as a temporary resident, proven by a registry certificate.
Sworn notarial statement of what you do in Guatemala.
Current Guatemalan guarantor letter, except religious ministers.
Refugees with temporary residence follow a lighter file.

routes.name: Permanent residence for Central Americans (1 year)
routes.summary: People born in another Central American country can apply for permanent residence after one year as a temporary resident.

other: Birth certificate showing birth in a Central American country.
Sworn notarial statement of your planned activity.
Proof of at least 1 year of temporary residence.

routes.name: Permanent residence through marriage, civil union or family of a Guatemalan
routes.summary: Spouses and civil union partners of Guatemalans can apply for permanent residence after 1 year or more of marriage or union, registered with RENAP. Relatives of a Guatemalan within legal degrees can also apply.

other: Marriage or union registered with RENAP for 1 year or more.
Relatives within legal degrees prove the tie with birth certificates.
Exact legal kinship degrees come from the Migration Code, which I did not re-read.

routes.name: Asylum and refugee protection
routes.summary: Asylum seekers can stay 30 days (extendable) while the case is reviewed. Recognized refugees and asylees get temporary residence right away. Guatemala must notify UNHCR before returning a denied applicant to danger.

other: Apply through IGM.
Recognized refugees and political asylees can get temporary residence with their recognition resolution, and later permanent residence.
The 30 day provisional stay comes from the Migration Code, not re-read here.

routes.name: Naturalization by concession
routes.summary: After five years registered as a resident foreigner, you can apply to the Foreign Ministry. The President decides at his discretion. Central American, Ibero-American and Spanish nationals have a privileged regime under Constitution Article 146.

other: No language test listed on the page.
Needs two Guatemalan witnesses, criminal and police records, tax and income certificates.
Dual citizenship rules not confirmed.

citizenship.note: Decision is discretionary. The process is free but you pay for the edicts published in the Diario Oficial.

routes.name: Temporary residence, worker paid from abroad
routes.summary: Workers with a foreign employer can get temporary residence by showing foreign pay of at least US$2,000 a month for the last year. With dependents the bar is US$3,000 a month. Staff of international NGOs or international organizations show a work letter or contract and health insurance instead.

income.note: US$3,000 a month with dependents. Shown with bank statements for the last year, or a certified accountant letter, signed and legalized or apostilled.

other: Remote work for a foreign employer fits here, but the rule does not use the words digital nomad.

routes.name: Temporary residence, self-employed worker
routes.summary: Self-employed foreigners can get temporary residence of up to 5 years. You file a sworn notarial statement of your planned activity and expected monthly income, plus tax registration and a business authorization.

other: Notarial sworn statement with activity, location, start date and monthly income projection.
RTU tax registration certificate.
Document from the competent body authorizing the business activity.
On renewal: accountant income letter, tax clearance and commercial registry papers.

routes.name: Temporary residence for family of a migrant worker
routes.summary: Spouses, partners and relatives within legal degrees of a migrant worker get temporary residence for the same term and status as the main applicant. They can file together or later.

other: Proof of the family tie plus the general residence documents.
A Guatemalan guarantor may be needed if they file after the worker.

stay.note: Same term as the main applicant.
